NASHR:v2p311/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p311/r2.speaker: القراء
NASHR:v2p311/r2.claim: All readers agree to open both ra and shin in the two earlier occurrences, in verses 18:10 and 18:24.
NASHR:v2p311/r2.anchor: الموضعين المتقدمين من هذه السورة، وهما وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا، ولأقرب من هذا رشدا أنهما بفتح الراء والشين

NASHR:v2p311/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p311/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p311/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jazari suggests the first two forms open for rhyme with nearby verse endings such as ʿajaban, ʿadadan, and aḥadan.
NASHR:v2p311/r5.anchor: الاتفاق على فتح الحرفين الأولين لمناسبة رءوس الآي وموازنتها لما قبل

BURHAN:v2p135/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p135/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p135/r9.claim: Voluntary prayer and the walk to the mosque count as gratitude; remaining good works after expiation are the lasting righteous deeds. Those with few sins and many good deeds are secure, while sins left beyond expiation are cause for fear.
BURHAN:v2p135/r9.anchor: وإنما يتبين بأن يبقى من العمل بعد الكفارة فضل وهو النافلة وهو المسمى بالباقيات الصالحات

DAMGHANI:v1p204/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p204/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p204/r6.anchor: الرشد الصواب قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

BURSEVI:v5p181/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p181/r1.claim: A future commitment is permissible only while conditioned on God's will; inwardly, choices and deeds all depend on God's will. When the qualification is remembered, one should say إن شاء الله.
BURSEVI:v5p181/r1.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من النهي أي : لا تقولن ذلك في حال من الأحوال إلا حال ملابسته بمشيئته تعالى

BURSEVI:v5p181/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p181/r2.claim: A report says the Prophet said إن شاء الله when the revelation arrived after his lapse.
BURSEVI:v5p181/r2.anchor: كما روى أنه عليه السلام لما نزل قال : "إن شاء الله"

BURSEVI:v5p181/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p181/r3.claim: He asks God for a clearer sign than the Cave youths' story as proof of prophethood; God gave him even more evident signs in distant prophetic histories and future events to the end of time.
BURSEVI:v5p181/r3.anchor: لشيء أقرب وأظهر من نبأ أصحاب الكهف من الآيات والدلائل الدالة على نبوتي

BURSEVI:v5p181/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181/r4.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v5p181/r4.claim: Since the Jews made the Cave story evidence for Muhammad's prophethood, God diminished its importance with this wording, as at the chapter's opening.
BURSEVI:v5p181/r4.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : لما جعل اليهود الحكاية عن أصحاب الكهف دالة على نبوته هون الله أمرها

BURSEVI:v5p181/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181/r5.speaker: السمرقندي
BURSEVI:v5p181/r5.claim: Another reading says that when someone forgets a thing, he should remember God and ask to be guided to something else that is closer, better, and more beneficial.

BURSEVI:v5p181/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181/r6.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v5p181/r6.claim: One may die before tomorrow or be obstructed while alive; without conditioning a promise on God's will, failure would be a lie, repugnant and unfitting for prophets.
BURSEVI:v5p181/r6.anchor: قال الإمام في تفسيره : والسبب في أنه لا بد من ذكر هذا القول هو أن الإنسان إذا قال

BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r1.claim: Abū al-Layth transmits via Abū Hurayra that Solomon vowed to visit one hundred wives to have warriors, forgot to say إن شاء الله, and all but one-half of a childless birth failed; the Prophet said the vow would have succeeded had he said it.
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r1.anchor: روي أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : قال سليمان بن داود

BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r2.claim: When people act as if they have independent will, God customarily brings about the opposite to show that only He has true will.
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r2.anchor: من لم يعلق فعله بمشيئته تعالى فإن من سنته أن يجرى الأمر على خلاف مشيئته

BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r3.claim: A hadith says complete faith includes making an exception in all speech, inwardly as well as outwardly; a merely verbal exception is ineffective.
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن من تمام إيمان العبد أن يستثني في كل حديثه"

BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r4.speaker: مولانا
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r4.claim: His couplet says that omitting an exception hardens intention, and the soul—not just passing words—must join the exception.
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r4.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : ترك استثناء مرادم قسوتيست نى همين كفتن كه عارض حالتيست

BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r5.speaker: روضة الخطيب
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r5.claim: A humorous story tells of a man who refused to say إن شاء الله while going to buy a donkey, lost his money, and later described the loss with repeated exceptions.
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r5.anchor: ومن لطائف "روضة الخطيب" أنه سئل رجل إلى أين؟ فقال

BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r6.claim: He permitted a delayed exception based on this verse, while most jurists rejected that rule because it would unsettle confessions, divorce, emancipation, and reports about the future.
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r6.anchor: واعلم أن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما جوز الاستثناء المنفصل بالآية المذكورة وعامة الفقهاء

BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r7.speaker: القرطبي
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r7.claim: The verse allows a delayed exception to retract and escape sin, but an exception changing a legal ruling must be connected to the original statement.
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r7.anchor: قال القرطبي في تأويل الآية : هذا في تدارك التبري والتخلص

BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r8.claim: At al-Manṣūr's court, Abū Ḥanīfa ruled an exception after a pause to an oath ineffective; Ibn Isḥāq appealed to Ibn ʿAbbās's view, but Abū Ḥanīfa explained its valid interpretation and warned that broad use could let people evade allegiance. Al-Manṣūr imprisoned Ibn Isḥāq.
BURSEVI:v5p181#2/r8.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : لا يعمل الاستثناء لأنه مقطوع وإنما ينفعه إذا كان متصلا

QASHANI:18:23-24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:23-24/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:23-24/r1.claim: God teaches the Prophet proper courtesy after forbidding disputation: speak of a future act only when God permits or while explicitly attaching it to His will.
QASHANI:18:23-24/r1.anchor: لا تقولن لما عزمت عليه من فعل إني فاعل ذلك في الزمان المستقبل إلا ملتبسا بمشيئة الله

QASHANI:18:23-24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:23-24/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:23-24/r2.claim: People should ascribe action to God’s will rather than their own, since they act through Him and His willing.
QASHANI:18:23-24/r2.anchor: لا تسند الفعل إلى إرادتك بل إلى إرادة الله، فتكون فاعلا به وبمشيئته

QASHANI:18:23-24/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:23-24/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:23-24/r3.claim: Remembering God means returning to His presence when heedlessness accompanies the ego’s emergence and shifting qualities.
QASHANI:18:23-24/r3.anchor: بالرجوع إليه والحضور { إذا نسيت } بالغفلة عند ظهور النفس والتلوين

QASHANI:18:23-24/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:23-24/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:23-24/r4.claim: The hoped-for better guidance is steadfast self-witnessing, freed from veils of attributes and from fluctuation.
QASHANI:18:23-24/r4.anchor: استقامة، وهو التمكين في الشهود الذاتي

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr retains the final yāʾ in the listed forms in both connection and pause, which the author calls the original analogical form.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamzah omit these yāʾs in both connection and pause; in connection they also omit yāʾ in non-rhyme forms such as يوم يأت.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r4.anchor: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة يحذفون الياء في الوصل والوقف

QIRAAT-ER:18:24:14#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:24:14#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:24:14#1/r1.claim: The full first-person yāʾ is retained in the standard form.
QIRAAT-ER:18:24:14#1/r1.anchor: Full yāʾ al-mutakallim retained — standard form with explicit first-person pronoun suffix

QIRAAT-ER:18:24:14#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:24:14#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:24:14#2/r1.claim: The pausal form has nūn sākina, while connected reading retains full yahdiyanī.
QIRAAT-ER:18:24:14#2/r1.anchor: Variant pausal form — nūn sākina in pause (yahdiyan) but full yahdiyanī in connected reading

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r6.claim: When forgetfulness comes, remembrance should strip one's purpose from the homeland of heedlessness; noticing one's own remembrance is itself a flaw.
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r6.anchor: فجرد بذكرك قصدك عن أوطان غفلتك

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r7.claim: Remember God after forgetting one's share in Him or forgetting everything besides Him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r7.anchor: ويقال واذكر ربك إذا نسيت حظك منه

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r8.claim: The youths were so absorbed they did not notice time passing; God nevertheless counted their breaths.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r3.claim: The Prophet said he would answer the next day without saying if God wills; revelation paused fifteen days, prompting Meccan rumors that his jinn inspiration had left him, then came with the answers and more.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r3.anchor: فقال: «غدا أخبركم» ولم يقل إن شاء الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r9.claim: The Prophet must not promise a future act without tying it to God’s will; the reported occasion is his answer to Quraysh that he would tell them tomorrow about the cave, al-Khiḍr, and the Spirit, without saying in shāʾ Allāh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r9.anchor: وتقدم في سبب النزول أنه عليه السلام حين سأله قريش عن أهل الكهف والخضر والروح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r10.claim: Reports say revelation was delayed fifteen days or forty days after the Prophet’s promise without qualification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r10.anchor: فتأخر عنه الوحي مدة. قيل: خمسة عشر يوما. وقيل: أربعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r11.claim: The exception cannot literally be part of the prohibited promise, so interpreters supply an omitted phrase that makes it a mention of God’s will rather than an exception inside the promised action.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r11.anchor: فاحتيج في تأويل هذا الظاهر إلى تقدير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies ‘unless you say, unless God wills’ or ‘unless you say if God wills’; the mention of God’s will is outside the prohibited promise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r12.anchor: تقديره إلا أن تقول إلا أن يشاء الله أو إلا أن تقول إن شاء الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attaches the exception to the prohibition, not to the promised action: either do not say it unless God wills you to say it, or say it only while invoking His will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r13.anchor: إلا أن يشاء الله متعلق بالنهي لا بقوله إني فاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers a third construction: إلا أن يشاء الله functions like a separate corrective phrase, as if the command said never promise it except under God’s will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r1.anchor: وفيه وجه ثالث وهو أن يكون إلا أن يشاء الله في معنى كلمة ثانية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r2.claim: This is divine instruction in proper etiquette after the Prophet said he would answer the next day without qualifying his promise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r2.anchor: وهذا نهي تأديب من الله لنبيه حين قال:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports a group that treats the exception as part of ولا تقولن; al-Ṭabarī cites this and rejects it as a corrupt interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقالت فرقة هو استثناء من قوله ولا تقولن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r4.claim: The verse is not about oaths, although exegetes discuss how it bears on making exceptions in an oath.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r4.anchor: وتكلم المفسرون في هذه الآية في الاستثناء في اليمين، وليست الآية في الأيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r5.claim: The apparent command is to remember God when one forgets; one proposed omitted object is a neglected commandment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r5.anchor: والظاهر أمره تعالى بذكر الله إذا عرض له نسيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r6.claim: Another interpretation says remembering God after forgetfulness can bring the forgotten matter back to mind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r6.anchor: وقيل واذكره إذا اعتراك النسيان ليذكرك المنسي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r7.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r7.claim: Qatāda applies the verse to performing a prayer missed through forgetfulness once it is remembered.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r7.anchor: وقد حمل قتادة ذلك على أداء الصلاة المنسية عند ذكرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r8.claim: Another interpretation urges glorification and seeking forgiveness when one forgets the phrase of exception, stressing the need to observe it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r8.anchor: وقيل: واذكر ربك بالتسبيح والاستغفار إذا نسيت كلمة الاستثناء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r9.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r9.claim: Ibn Jubayr says to remember God’s will after forgetting to say it, even if one remembers a day, month, or year later.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r9.anchor: قاله ابن جبير. قال: ولو بعد يوم أو شهر أو سنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r10.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says one may remember after the period has passed, like telling someone to remember something after a friend has finished praying.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r10.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: بعد تقضي النسيان كما تقول: اذكر لعبد الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r11.claim: لأقرب من هذا likely refers to what was forgotten: ask God to guide one to another, nearer and more beneficial course; forgetting may be for the better, as 2:106 says.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r11.anchor: والإشارة بقوله لأقرب من هذا إلى الشيء المنسي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī instead makes ‘this’ the cave structure and reads the prayer as a request for proofs of prophethood clearer than the cave sign; God then gave the Prophet greater signs through prophetic stories and unseen knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p162/r12.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وهذا إشارة إلى بناء أهل الكهف، ومعناه لعل الله يؤتيني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r1.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj had already interpreted the prayer as asking for clearer evidence of the Prophet’s mission than the cave sign.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r1.anchor: وهذا تقدمه إليه الزجاج قال المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the Prophet hoped to receive answers before the deadline and for guidance to be hastened.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r2.anchor: عسى أن يعرفني جواب مسائلكم قبل الوقت الذي حددته لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r3.speaker: محمد الكوفي المفسر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r3.claim: Muḥammad al-Kūfī says everyone who forgot to say in shāʾ Allāh is instructed to say these words as expiation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r3.anchor: هي بألفاظها مما أمر أن يقولها كل من لم يستثن

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r2.claim: When one forgets self and creation, one remembers God; in that remembrance, creation and self are seen as having no independent existence.
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : إذا نسيت نفسك والخلق ، فاذكرني فإن الأذكار لا تمازج ذكري

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r3.claim: If you have forgotten remembrance through God, remember Him.
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r3.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : إذا نسيت ذكري بي فاذكرني

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r4.claim: When you forget all others, draw near to God through remembrance.
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r4.anchor: قال جعفر : إذا نسيت الأغيار فتقرب إلي بالأذكار

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r5.claim: Remembrance is the rememberer's annihilation within it, and remembrance occurs through witnessing the Remembered.
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r5.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : الذكر فناء الذاكر فيه ، والذكر في مشاهدة المذكور

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r6.claim: When connection is severed and separation remains from witnessing, one remembers God through the reality of His remembrance.
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ﴿ واذكر ربك إذا نسيت ﴾ إذا انقطعت علائق الاتصال وبقيت الانفصال

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r7.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r7.claim: The address to remember God is not for realized people, since the Real is not forgotten; life and existence themselves remember Him.
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r7.anchor: وقال الشبلي رحمه الله في قوله : ﴿ واذكر ربك ﴾ : ما هذا خطاب أهل الحقيقة وأنى ينسى المحق الحق

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r8.claim: The command means repent to God when you sin.
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم في هذه الآية : تب إلى ربك إذا عصيت

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r9.claim: The great ones forget when the presence of the Real overtakes them.
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : نسيان الأكابر إذا ورد المحق عليهم بحضوره

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r10.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r10.claim: True remembrance is annihilation in the Remembered, beyond remembrance itself; when remembrance is forgotten, the Remembered becomes one's attribute.
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r10.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : حقيقة الذكر الفناء بالمذكور عن الذكر

SULAMI:v1p409#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#4/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p409#4/r1.claim: A station above remembrance is God's remembering the servant first, stripping away attributes through His remembrance before the servant remembers Him.
SULAMI:v1p409#4/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله في هذه الآية : إن فوق الذكر منزلة هو أقرب رشدا ذكره له

AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r1.claim: إلا أن يشاء الله means unless you say إن شاء الله; in a long statement, an indication of this kind suffices because one part points to the whole.
AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r1.anchor: أي: إلا أن تقول: "إن شاء الله" فأجزأ من ذلك هذا،

FARRA:v2p138/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p138/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p138/r2.claim: إلا أن يشاء الله means to say إن شاء الله; the omitted sense is not to promise tomorrow except with God's will.
FARRA:v2p138/r2.anchor: إلا أن تقول: إن شاء الله

FARRA:v2p138/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p138/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v2p138/r3.claim: If someone swears and forgets to make an exception, Ibn Abbas says to make it when remembered, provided the oath has not yet been broken.
FARRA:v2p138/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إذا حلفت فنسيت أن تستثني فاستثن متى ما ذكرت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya, following al-Tabari's rebuttal, calls the exception for God's will corrupt; Alusi says this is unfair and the exception properly attaches to the prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r1.anchor: وقول ابن عطية اغترارا برد الطبري أنه من الفساد بحيث كان الواجب أن لا يحكى خروج عن الإنصاف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r2.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r2.claim: The exception can mean do not say it in any state except while mentioning God's will, since a spoken promise cannot literally be joined to the divine will; another analysis makes it a state exception with an elided bāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r2.anchor: إن التباس القول بحقيقة المشيئة محال فبقي أن يكون بذكرها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r3.claim: The exception may instead refer to times, with God's will interpreted as permission: do not speak until God authorizes it; it may also be a disconnected exception signaling a permanent prohibition because the time of God's will is unknown.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المستثنى من أعم الأوقات أي لا تقولن ذلك في وقت من الأوقات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r4.claim: The permanent-prohibition reading is not that God never wills the Prophet to speak because such speech is intrinsically bad; limiting the rule to revelation still does not follow from the text's indefinite noun under negation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r4.anchor: لأن القبح فيما نحن فيه على إطلاقه غير مسلم والتخصيص بما يتعلق بالوحي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#3/r5.claim: The apparent reading attaches the exception to the prohibition, and the Prophet's community is included in the address; it cannot sensibly attach to the declaration that he will act, because either proposed sense conflicts with the prohibition.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r1.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r1.claim: Al-Khafaji rejects attaching the exception to nonperformance: Sunnis and Muʿtazilites alike cannot make that a coherent prohibition, since God can prevent an intended act through death or another impediment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r1.anchor: وقال الخفاجي : إذا كان الاستثناء متعلقا بأني فاعل والمشيئة متعلقة بالعدم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r2.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r2.claim: He also rejects reading the verse as forbidding a Muʿtazilite to claim independent authorship whenever God's will does not accompany the act.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r2.anchor: فيضيفها لنفسه قائلا إن لم تقترن مشيئة الله تعالى بالفعل فأنا فاعله استقلالا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r3.speaker: الاعتراض على المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r3.claim: A familiar objection says that if God wills only obedience, a debtor who vows to pay tomorrow if God wills must be perjured when he fails to pay, making the exception ineffective; it is like a condition whose condition occurs.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r3.anchor: لو كان كذلك لوجب فيما إذا قال : الذي عليه دين لغيره قد طالبه به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r4.speaker: المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r4.claim: Al-Murtaḍā distinguishes exceptions that suspend the legal force of oaths, contracts, and reports; this use may be retrospective but is unsuitable for sins because it displays reliance on God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r4.anchor: بأن للاستثناء الداخل في الكلام وجوها مختلفة فقد يدخل في الأيمان والطلاق والعتاق

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r5.speaker: المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r5.claim: A second use in permitted matters asks God to enable the act and preserve the existing state; al-Murtaḍā considers this possible in the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r5.anchor: وقد يدخل في الكلام ويراد به التسهيل والأقدار والتخلية والبقاء على ما هو عليه من الأحوال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r6.speaker: المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r6.claim: A third use merely expresses reliance on God without deciding whether the statement is true or false, and could also fit the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r6.anchor: وقد يدخل لمجرد غرض الانقطاع إلى الله تعالى ويكون على هذا غير معتمد به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r7.speaker: المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r7.claim: A fourth use seeks divine grace and facilitation, which applies only to obedience and cannot explain the verse's broader scope; if the debtor intended another sense, he need not be perjured.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r7.anchor: وقد يدخل ويراد به اللطف والتسهيل وهذا يختص بالطاعات ولا يصح أن تحمل الآية عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the objection and this answer are unpersuasive, and the Muʿtazilite position can be refuted without them.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r8.anchor: والانصاف أن الاعتراض ليس بشيء والرد عليهم غني عن مثل ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r9.speaker: السيرافي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r9.claim: Using exception for qualification by saying if God wills, and for qualification by a condition generally, is established in Arabic usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r9.anchor: إطلاق الاستثناء على التقييد بإن شاء الله تعالى بل على التقييد بالشرط مطلقا ثابت في اللغة والاستعمال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r10.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r10.claim: Al-Rāghib defines exception as removing what a preceding general statement entails, as in the verse about what may be eaten, or what a particular utterance entails, as in a conditional divorce.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r10.anchor: وقال الراغب : الاستثناء دفع ما يوجبه عموم سابق كما في قوله تعالى : ( قل لا أجد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r11.claim: The Prophetic report says that whoever swears to something and says if God wills has made an exception; al-Ālūsī therefore rejects explanations that call the phrase an exception only because of its Quranic wording or resemblance.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r11.anchor: من حلف على شيء فقال : إن شاء الله تعالى فقد استثنى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r12.claim: Remembering the Lord means remembering His will, with an omitted genitive; the preceding command is to say if God wills, as the Prophet did when this verse came down.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r12.anchor: أي مشيئة ربك فالكلام على حذف مضاف وذكر مشيئته تعالى على ما يدل عليه ما قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r13.claim: Forgetting means an inadvertent omission; the command applies upon remembering, not during forgetfulness, and requires recovery whether the interval is short or long.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r13.anchor: إذا فرط منك نسيان ذلك ثم تذكرته فإنه مادام ناسيا لا يؤمر بالذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās held that a person may add the exception even after a year; this is also reported from the Imams of the Prophet's family and as one narration from Aḥmad.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r14.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه كان يرى الاستثناء ولو بعد سنة ويقرأ الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r15.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r15.claim: Ibn Jubayr says a person who swore and forgot to except retains the right of exception for a month.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r15.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جبير في رجل حلف ونسي أن يستثني قال : له ثنياه إلى شهر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r16.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r16.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, reporting from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, allows the exception for as long as it takes to milk a camel.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r16.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق عمرو بن دينار عن عطاء أنه قال : من حلف على يمين فله الثنيا حلب ناقة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r17.speaker: طاوس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r17.claim: Ṭāwūs limits the exception to the time a person remains in the same sitting.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r17.anchor: وكان طاوس يقول ما دام في مجلسه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r18.speaker: إبراهيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r18.claim: Ibrāhīm says the exception is available only while the person is still speaking.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r18.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم أيضا عن إبراهيم قال : يستثنى ما دام في كلامه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r19.speaker: عامة الفقهاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r19.claim: Most jurists require the exception to be connected to the oath; allowing it after any delay would undermine the finality of acknowledgments, divorce, emancipation, and truthful or false statements.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r19.anchor: وعامة الفقهاء على اشتراط اتصال الاستثناء في عدم الحنث ولو صح جواز الفصل وعدم تأثيره في الأحكام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r20.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r20.claim: In a story, Abū Ḥanīfa answers al-Manṣūr's objection to his disagreement with Ibn ʿAbbās by warning that delayed exceptions would let people leave a pledge of allegiance and then break it; al-Manṣūr approves the answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p248/r20.anchor: فقال له أبو حنيفة : هذا يرجع إليك إنك تأخذ البيعة بالأيمان أفترضى أن يخرجوا من عندك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r1.claim: A traveler from the Maghrib hears two Baghdad vegetable sellers debate delayed exceptions: one argues that Job would have been told to except if Ibn ʿAbbās were right, since the remedy in the verse about his oath came after a year.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r1.anchor: ومن غريب ما يحكى أن رجلا من علماء المغرب أحب أن يرى علماء بغداد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r2.claim: The traveler returns home impressed that even a street seller could challenge Ibn ʿAbbās, and infers how learned Baghdad's scholars must be.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r2.anchor: رأيت من يبيع على رأسه في الطرقات من أهلها بلغ مبلغا من العلم يعترض به على ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī says such an objection is excessive even from a vegetable seller and cautions that God knows whether the anecdote is authentic.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r3.anchor: والانصاف أن هذا الاعتراض على علامة يستكثر ممن يبيع البقل والله تعالى أعلم بصحة النقل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r4.claim: The apparent verse and report may seem to support Ibn ʿAbbās, but the required recovery is only a renewed declaration of dependence on God, not a delayed change to legal effect; the passage does not address legal rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r4.anchor: إن التدارك فيما يرجع إلى تفويض العبد يحصل بذكره بعد التنبه أما في التأثير في الحكم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r5.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says that one who forgot the exception should make it when remembering, but that this privilege belongs only to the Prophet; others may except only as part of an oath.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال في الآية : إذا نسيت الاستثناء فاستثن إذا ذكرت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r6.claim: An alternative says the later words attach to an implied recurring statement: whenever one forgets God, remember Him upon recollection, or say if God wills when announcing a future act; al-Ālūsī finds this far from the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250/r6.anchor: وقيل ليس في الآية والخبر أن الاستثناء المتدارك من القول السابق بل من مقدر مدلول به عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r1.claim: One interpretation makes remembering the Lord mean glorifying and seeking forgiveness after forgetting the exception, urging it by implying that its omission merits repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r1.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المعنى واذكر ربك بالتسبيح والاستغفار إذا نسيت الاستثناء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r2.claim: Another reads the command as remembering God and His punishment after leaving an instruction, to prompt correction; forgetfulness here is figurative for leaving something.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r2.anchor: وقيل المعنى واذكر ربك وعقابه إذا تركت بعض ما أمرك به ليبعثك ذلك على التدارك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r3.claim: A further reading says to remember God when forgetfulness comes so He may remind the person of what was forgotten; it treats forgetfulness as intransitive, but connects poorly to the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r3.anchor: أو اذكر ربك إذا عرض لك نسيان ليذكرك المنسي و ( نيست ) على هذا منزل منزلة اللازم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r4.claim: Qatāda takes the verse to command making up a missed prayer when one remembers it; al-Ālūsī says this seems to be his intended reading and has the same weak contextual connection.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r4.anchor: وحمل قتادة الآية على أداء الصلاة المنسية عند ذكرها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r5.claim: If Qatāda instead infers prayer's make-up from the command to remember a forgotten exception, the analogy is more plausible because prayer merits greater concern, though this is not the apparent report.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r5.anchor: وإن أراد أنها تدل على الأمر بقضاء الصلاة المنسية عند ذكرها لما أنها دلت على الأمر بذكر الاستثناء المنسي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r6.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r6.claim: ʿIkrima interprets the verse as remembering God when angry, since anger can cause forgetfulness; al-Ālūsī regards its contextual problem as like the prior interpretations.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان وغيرهما عن عكرمة أنه قال في الآية : أي اذكر ربك إذا غضبت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads the prayer for guidance as asking God to grant a sign more evident than the account of the Companions of the Cave, proving the Prophet's mission and guiding people.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r7.anchor: أي يوفقني ( لأقرب من هذا ( أي لشيء أقرب وأظهر من نبأ أصحاب الكهف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r8.claim: God later gave the Prophet clearer signs, including accounts of distant prophets and future events through the Resurrection; the wording also gently reduces the cave story's apparent wonder, as did the opening question.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r8.anchor: وقد فعل ذلك عز وجل حيث آتاه من الآيات البينات ما هو أعظم من ذلك وأبين كقصص الأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r9.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r9.claim: One syntactic proposal links the prayer for guidance back to the command to recall when the youths took refuge in the cave: tell that story and hope for a clearer sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p250#2/r9.anchor: على العامل في قوله تعالى ( إذ أوى الفتية إلى الكهف ) كأنه قيل اذكر إذ أوى الفتية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r1.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r1.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī links the guidance prayer to remembering God: ask God to remind the Prophet of a forgotten matter, and if not, to guide him to something nearer and more beneficial; al-Ālūsī finds this closer syntactically but distant in other respects.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r1.anchor: وقال الجبائي : هو متعلق بقوله تعالى ( واذكر ربك ) إلى آخره والمعنى عنده ادع ربك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r2.claim: Another proposal links it to the preceding commands and prohibitions: hope for guidance to what is more beneficial than their instruction; al-Ālūsī judges this strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r2.anchor: وقيل : إنه متعلق بالمتعاطفات قبله و ( هذا ) إشارة إلى ما تضمنته من الخير أمرا ونهيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says God may reveal answers to the questioners before the promised time and hasten guidance; al-Ālūsī says the meaning cannot be derived and would make the Quran like a riddle.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري : معنى الآية عسى أن يعرفني ربي جواب مسائلكم قبل الوقت الذي حددته لكم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r4.speaker: رجل من أهل الكوفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r4.claim: An unnamed Kufan, transmitted through Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān and his father and attributed by Abū Ḥayyān to Muḥammad al-Kūfī, says repentance for forgetting the exception is to recite the guidance prayer; al-Ālūsī says it has no evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251/r4.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي من طريق المعتمر بن سليمان قال : سمعت أبي يحدث عن رجل من أهل الكوفة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r1.claim: An esoteric interpretation says to remember God after forgetting the whole universe, including oneself, because remembrance becomes pure only then.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r1.anchor: قيل أي إذا نسيت الكون بأسره حتى نفسك فإن الذكر لا يصفو إلا حينئذ

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r2.speaker: الجنيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r2.claim: Al-Junayd reads the command as remembering after forgetting remembrance itself; true remembrance is annihilation in the Remembered apart from the act of remembering.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r2.anchor: وقيل إذا نسيت الذكر ومن هنا قال الجنيد قدس سره : حقيقة الذكر الفناء بالمذكور عن الذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r3.speaker: الجنيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r3.claim: Al-Junayd says a station above remembrance is nearer to guidance: God describes and remembers the servant before the servant remembers Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r3.anchor: وقال قدس سره في قوله تعالى ( وقل عسى أن يهديني ربي لأقرب من هذا رشدا ( إن فوق الذكر منزلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.claim: One should not promise to act tomorrow without adding God's will; after promising answers to Meccan questions the next day without this phrase, revelation paused for days.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن أهل مكة سألوه عن الروح وعن أصحاب الكهف وعن ذي القرنين فقال: أخبركم غدا ولم يقل إن شاء الله فلبث الوحي أياما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.claim: If one forgets to say the exception, one should add it upon remembering.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن: معناه إذا نسيت الاستثناء ثم ذكرت فاستثن.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.claim: He allows a belated exception even after a year; al-Hasan allows it in the same gathering, some only after a short interval, while another group requires it to be connected to the original speech.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.anchor: وجوز ابن عباس الاستثناء المنقطع وإن كان إلى سنة وجوزه الحسن ما دام في المجلس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.claim: He interprets remembering the Lord after forgetting as remembering God when angry.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: معنى الآية: واذكر ربك إذا غضبت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.claim: He cites a Gospel saying that if the son of Adam remembers God when angry, God will remember him when angry.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.anchor: وقال وهب: مكتوب في الإنجيل: ابن آدم اذكرني حين تغضب أذكرك حين أغضب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r6.claim: They apply the command to prayer; Anas reports the Prophet said a forgotten prayer should be performed upon remembering.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي: هذا في الصلاة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r7.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction that whoever forgets a prayer should pray it when remembering.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة عن أنس قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r1.claim: The Prophet asks his Lord to keep him on a more direct and better-guided path.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r1.anchor: أي: يثبتني على طريق هو أقرب إليه وأرشد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r2.claim: Another reading makes the request for guidance an appeal for something better than recalling what was forgotten.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r2.anchor: وقيل: أمر الله نبيه أن يذكره إذا نسي شيئا ويسأله أن يهديه لما هو خير له من ذكر ما نسيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r3.claim: When opponents asked about the Cave story to challenge him, the Prophet was to say God would give him clearer proofs of his mission than that story; later knowledge of the unseen did so.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r3.anchor: ويقال: هو أن القوم لما سألوه عن قصة أصحاب الكهف على وجه العناد أمره الله عز وجل أن يخبرهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r4.claim: Another view takes this as a formula to say with God's will after remembering a forgotten exception, and as repentance if one forgot the formula.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذا شيء أمر أن يقوله مع قوله "إن شاء الله" إذا ذكر الاستثناء بعد النسيان

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas allows a delayed exception as late as a year, provided the speaker has not broken an oath.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ولو بعد سنة ما لم يحنث

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r4.speaker: عامة الفقهاء
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r4.claim: Most jurists disagree: allowing a year-late exception would destabilize acknowledgements, divorce, emancipation, and truth or falsehood judgments.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r4.anchor: وعامة الفقهاء على خلافه لأنه لو صح ذلك لم يتقرر إقرار ولا طلاق

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r5.claim: The verse and report do not prove that an exception can retroactively amend earlier speech; the command may instead refer to an implied new statement.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r5.anchor: وليس في الآية والخبر أن الاستثناء المتدارك به من القول السابق

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r6.claim: Remembering God after forgetting may mean praising and seeking forgiveness, recalling His punishment to motivate correction, or asking Him to restore what was forgotten.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى واذكر ربك بالتسبيح والاستغفار إذا نسيت

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r7.claim: The prayer asks for a clearer proof of prophethood than the sleepers' story; alternatively, it seeks nearer guidance or good than what was forgotten.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:23-24/r7.anchor: لأقرب رشدا وأظهر دلالة على أني نبي من نبأ أصحاب الكهف

NAHHAS:v2p453/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p453/r2.claim: ‘Unless God wills’ is an accusative of disconnected exception.
NAHHAS:v2p453/r2.anchor: إلا أن يشاء الله . . . . ) ^ [ 24 ] نصب على الاستثناء المنقطع

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r7.claim: When one forgets to make an exception, remembering God and invoking His will upon recollection is not culpable.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r7.anchor: حال النسيان { إذا نسيت } الاستثناء بالاستعانة والتوكل عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r8.speaker: الطبراني عن ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r8.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits from Ibn Abbas that this instruction was specific to the Prophet; others may attach an exception only to an oath.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r8.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني في معجمه الأوسط في ترجمة محمد بن الحارث الجبيلي

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r9.claim: Aqرب is the comparative from the intransitive قَرُبَ, unlike the transitive root used in prohibitions against approaching adultery or orphan property.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r9.anchor: و ( اقرب ) أفعل تفضيل من قرب - بضم الراء - من الشيء , لازم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r10.claim: The nearer guidance is to infer prophethood, divine oneness, and resurrection from broad or frequent signs rather than this rare, demanding detail.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r10.anchor: بالأمور الكلية أو الجزيئات القريبة المتكررة , ولا بهذا الأمر الجزئي النادر المتعب

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r1.claim: After Quraysh asked about the sleepers, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit on Jewish advice, the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying إن شاء الله; Gabriel was delayed fifteen days, then explained the omission and brought the answers.
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r1.anchor: فقال: أخبركم بذلك غدا ولم يقل إن شاء الله

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r2.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r2.claim: Gabriel explained that his delay followed the Prophet's failure to qualify his promise with God's will.
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r2.anchor: فقال: بتركك الاستثناء ألا تقول: إن شاء الله قال: (ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله)

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r4.claim: When the answer matched what the Jews had said about the third question, Quraysh called the two revelations cooperating sorceries, meaning the Torah and Quran, and rejected both.
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r4.anchor: (قالوا: سحران تظاهرا) (القصص آية 48) تعاونا - يعني التوراة والفرقان -

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r5.claim: The Prophet warned that every prophet warned his people about the Dajjal; he would certainly emerge among this final community, and God would be each Muslim's protector.
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r5.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني عن أبي أمامة قال: خطبنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما فكان أكثر خطبته ذكر الدجال

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r6.claim: The Dajjal will emerge between Iraq and Syria and devastate lands to either side; he will claim prophethood while denying that any prophet follows Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r6.anchor: وإن يخرج من خلة بين العراق والشام وعاث يمينا وعاث شمالا

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r7.claim: The word كافر will appear between the Dajjal's eyes and every believer will read it; believers are instructed to recite the opening passages of al-Kahf against him.
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r7.anchor: وإنه مكتوب بين عينيه كافر يقرؤه كل مؤمن فمن لقية منكم فليتفل في وجهه

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r8.claim: The Dajjal will kill one person and revive him, but will not be able to exercise that power over another person.
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r8.anchor: وإنه يسلط على نفس من بني آدم فيقتلها ثم يحييها وإنه لا يعدو ذلك

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r9.claim: The Dajjal's apparent paradise is fire and his fire is paradise; a believer tested by the fire should close his eyes and seek God's help, and it will be cool and safe like the fire for Abraham.
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r9.anchor: فناره جنة وجنته نارا فمن ابتلي بناره فليغمض عينيه وليستعن بالله

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r10.claim: The Dajjal's forty days include one like a year, one like a month, one like a week, and a final day like an ordinary day.
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r10.anchor: وإن أيامه أربعون يوما يوم كسنة ويوم كشهر ويوم كجمعة ويوم كالأيام

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r1.claim: On Jewish advice Quraysh asked the Prophet about the Cave sleepers, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; he promised to answer the next day without an exception, and Gabriel did not come until God willed.
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r1.anchor: فكتبوا إلى قريش: أن سلوه عن أمر أصحاب الكهف وعن ذي القرنين وعن الروح

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r2.claim: The Prophet explained that the delay distressed him because he had no knowledge of the answers before revelation; a puppy in his house was also why Gabriel did not enter.
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r2.anchor: قال: ألم ترنا لا ندخل بيتا فيه كلب ولا صورة - وكان في البيت جرو كلب -

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet made an oath, forty nights passed, then this verse came and he added the exception after forty nights.
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حلف على يمين فمضى له أربعون ليلة

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas allowed an exception even after a year, interpreting remembering one's Lord as making the exception once remembered.
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يرى الاستثناء ولو بعد سنة ثم قرأ {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت} قال: إذا ذكرت

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r5.claim: If one forgets to say إن شاء الله when promising to do something, Ibn Abbas says to say it upon remembering.
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية قال: إذا نسيت أن تقول لشيء إني أفعله فنسيت أن تقول إن شاء الله

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliya says to make the exception when one remembers.
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله: {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت} قال: تستثني إذا ذكرت

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r7.claim: Said ibn Jubayr lets someone who forgot an exception to an oath add it within a month.
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في رجل حلف ونسي أن يستثني قال له: ثنياه إلى شهر وقرأ {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت}

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r8.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r8.claim: Ata describes the time for adding the exception as the time needed to milk a camel.
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r8.anchor: عن عطاء أنه قال: من حلف على يمين فله الثنيا حلب ناقة

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r1.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r1.claim: Tawus says an oath's exception may be added while the speaker remains in the same sitting.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r1.anchor: وكان طاوس يقول: ما دام في مجلسه

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r2.claim: Ibrahim likewise limits the exception to the time one remains in the same utterance.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: يستثني مادام في كلامه

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the delayed exception was a dispensation specific to the Prophet; others may only attach it to the oath itself.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت} قال: إذا نسيت الاستثناء فاستثن إذا ذكرت قال: هي خاصة لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r4.claim: Ibn Umar says a connected exception prevents an oath from being broken, while an unconnected one does not.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: كل استثناء موصول فلا حنث على صاحبه وإذا كان غير موصول فهو حانث

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r5.claim: The Prophet says whoever makes an oath conditional on God's will may carry it out or withdraw without breaking it.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من حلف فقال: إن شاء الله فإن شاء مضى وإن شاء رجع غير حانث

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r6.claim: Solomon vowed to visit ninety wives so each would bear a fighter; he forgot the exception despite the angel's reminder, and only one half-formed child was born. The Prophet said the exception would have fulfilled his wish without breaking the oath.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: قال سليمان بن داود عليهما السلام: لأطوقن الليلة على تسعين امرأة

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r7.claim: Ikrima interprets remembering one's Lord as remembering while angry.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله: {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت} قال: إذا غضبت

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r8.claim: Hasan explains the verse as referring to when one failed to say إن شاء الله.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r8.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت} قال: إذا لم تقل إن شاء الله

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r9.speaker: أبو الحارث
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r9.claim: A Kufan Quran reciter says that after forgetting God's will, one repents by saying the following prayer for closer guidance.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r9.anchor: سمعت أبا الحارث عن رجل من أهل الكوفة كان يقرأ القرآن في الآية قال: إذا نسي الإنسان أن يقول إن شاء الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق والطبري والواحدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r1.claim: Reports say the polytheists asked about the sleepers and Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying ‘if God wills’; revelation was delayed fifteen days, or three in another report.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r1.anchor: ما رواه ابن إسحاق والطبري في أول هذه السورة والواحدي في سورة مريم : أن المشركين لما سألوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur treats the delayed revelation as a subtle reproach, followed by a direct prohibition against promising future action without qualifying it by God’s will.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r2.anchor: فكان تأخير الوحي إليه بالجواب عتابا رمزيا من الله لرسوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r3.speaker: البخاري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r3.claim: Bukhari’s report about Solomon says he vowed to visit one hundred women in a night so each would bear a fighter, but only one gave birth to half a boy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r3.anchor: كما عاتب سليمان عليه السلام فيما رواه البخاري : ( أن سليمان قال : لأطوفن الليلة على مائة امرأة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r4.claim: The Prophet forgot to say ‘if God wills’ when promising an answer; after relating the story, God forbade unqualified promises, as with Solomon’s forgotten qualification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295/r4.anchor: فإن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما سئل عن أهل الكهف وعد بالإجابة ونسي أن يقول : ( إن شاء الله ) كما نسي سليمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes ‘unless God wills’ as an exception from the prohibition itself: one may make the statement only if God permits it, with the omitted object supplied from context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r1.anchor: فمقتضى كلام الزمخشري أنه من بقية جملة النهي ، أي هو استثناء من حكم النهي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r2.speaker: الكسائي والأخفش والفراء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash, and al-Farrāʾ take the exception from ‘I will do that tomorrow’: the promise is allowed when accompanied by saying ‘if God wills.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r2.anchor: ومقتضى كلام الكسائي والأخفش والفراء أنه مستثنى من جملة { إني فاعل ذلك غدا } ، فيكون مستثنى من كلام النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r3.claim: The verse honors the Prophet by answering his question, teaching prophetic etiquette, and postponing the rebuke until after answering so he would not mistake correction for refusal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r3.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه الآية كرامة للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم من ثلاث جهات : الأولى : أنه أجاب سؤله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r4.speaker: حكيم بن حزام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r4.claim: In a report, the Prophet gave Ḥakīm repeatedly when he asked, then advised him about taking wealth freely; Ḥakīm understood the counsel was ethical and vowed not to take from anyone else.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p295#2/r4.anchor: ومثاله ما في الصحيح : أن حكيم بن حزام قال : ( سألت رسول الله فأعطاني ثم سألته فأعطاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r1.claim: The lām in li-shayʾ is causal, meaning ‘for something you intend to do’; dhālika refers to that intended action, including answering their question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r1.anchor: فنظم الآية أن اللام في قوله : { لشيء } ليست اللام التي يتعدى بها فعل القول إلى المخاطب بل هي لام العلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r2.claim: Ghadā is a figurative term for future time, not necessarily the next day, as in Zuhayr’s contrast among today, yesterday, and tomorrow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r2.anchor: مرادا بها اليوم الذي يلي يومه ، ولكنه مستعمل في معنى الزمان المستقبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r3.claim: Although the apparent scope is future plans, most jurists say adding ‘if God wills’ releases an oath without expiation; they extend the broad wording to vows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r3.anchor: وظاهر الآية اقتصار إعمالها على الإخبار بالعزم على فعل في المستقبل دون ما كان من الكلام إنشاء مثل الأيمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r4.speaker: ابن القاسم وأشهب وابن عبد الحكم عن مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r4.claim: These transmit from Mālik that ‘remember your Lord when you forget’ concerns remembering God after forgetfulness, not oath exceptions; the oath ruling comes from Sunna, as also held by Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r4.anchor: وروى ابن القاسم وأشهب وابن عبد الحكم عن مالك أن قوله : { ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل } الخ . . إنما قصد بذلك ذكر الله عند السهو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r5.claim: ʿUmar says the best remembrance of God is to remember Him when encountering His commands and prohibitions, supporting the meaning of remembrance as compliance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p297/r5.anchor: كما قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه : ( أفضل من ذكر الله باللسان ذكر الله عند أمره ونهيه )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r1.claim: Addressing God as ‘your Lord’ rather than using the divine name carries a special gentleness; the object of forgetting is the prohibition just mentioned.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r1.anchor: وفي تعريف الجلالة بلفظ الرب مضافا إلى ضمير المخاطب دون اسم الجلالة العلم من كمال الملاطفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r2.claim: Some jurists read ‘remember your Lord when you forget’ as permission to add an oath exception upon remembering, without a time limit; Ibn ʿAbbās permits even a long delay.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : لا تحديد بمدة بل ولو طال ما بين اليمين والثنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r3.claim: The majority reject using this verse to permit delayed oath exceptions, arguing that the Sunna states otherwise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r3.anchor: والجمهور على أن قوله : { واذكر ربك إذا نسيت } لا دلالة فيه على جواز تأخير الثنيا ، واستدلوا بأن السنة وردت بخلافه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r4.claim: After fulfilling the promised answer about the sleepers, God rebukes the Prophet for engaging questions beyond the mission without permission and directs him to seek more important guidance in revealed law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r4.anchor: لما أبر الله وعد نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم الذي وعده المشركين أن يبين لهم أمر أهل الكهف فأوحاه إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r5.claim: ‘Say, perhaps my Lord will guide me’ may continue the command not to dispute their number, or be a prayer joined to remembering God after forgetting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جملة وقل عسى أن يهدين ربي } عطفا على جملة { واذكر ربك إذا نسيت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r6.claim: Rushdan either specifies the comparative relation in ‘closer than this’ or serves as an absolute object describing the kind of guidance sought.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p298/r6.anchor: وانتصب { رشدا } على تمييز نسبة التفضيل من قوله : { لأقرب من هذا } . ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا على أنه مفعول مطلق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r6.claim: The phrase 'except if God wills' has an implied command to say 'if God wills'; it directs mention of God's will rather than serving as an exception from the prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r6.anchor: تقديره: إلا أن تقول إلا أن يشاء الله، أو إلا أن تقول إن شاء الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r1.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r1.claim: Al-Tabari reports and rejects the reading that 'except if God wills' is an exception to the prohibition itself; the author says it is so unsound that it should not have been cited.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r1.anchor: وهذا قول حكاه الطبري ورد عليه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan say 'remember your Lord when you forget' means to say the exception later if you forgot it initially, joining those who condition their plans on God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن معناه، والإشارة به إلى الاستثناء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r3.claim: Ikrima interprets 'when you forget' as 'when you become angry.'
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة: المعنى واذكر ربك إذا غضبت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r4.claim: Although the verse concerns the general practice of saying 'if God wills,' Malik and many jurists say an oath's exception only works and cancels expiation when joined to the oath.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r4.anchor: أما مالك رحمه الله وجميع أصحابه، فيما علمت، وكثير من العلماء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r5.speaker: عطاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r5.claim: Ata allows an oath's exception up to the time needed to milk a large-yield camel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r5.anchor: وقال عطاء له أن يستثني في قدر حلب الناقة الغزيرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r6.claim: Qatada allows the exception before the oath is spoken.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة إن استثنى قبل أن يقول أو يتكلم فله ثنياه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r7.speaker: ابن حنبل وابن راهويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r7.claim: Ibn Hanbal and Ibn Rahawayh allow the exception while the person is still engaged in the matter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r7.anchor: وقال ابن حنبل له الاستثناء ما دام في ذلك الأمر، وقاله ابن راهويه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r8.speaker: طاوس والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r8.claim: Tawus and al-Hasan allow it while the oath-taker remains in the same sitting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r8.anchor: وهذا قول حكاه الطبري ورد عليه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r9.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r9.claim: Ibn Jubayr allows a delayed exception for up to four months.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r9.anchor: وقال ابن جبير ينفع الاستثناء بعد أربعة أشهر فقط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to allow a delayed exception even after a year; Mujahid says two years and Abu al-Aliya says indefinitely.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ينفع الاستثناء ولو بعد سنة، وقال مجاهد بعد سنتين،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r11.claim: Al-Tabari interprets Ibn Abbas as meaning that a person may later join the category of those who remember to qualify their plans, not that expiation disappears; a Prophetic report requires expiation when one chooses a better course after an oath.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r11.anchor: إنما أراد ابن عباس أنه ينفع في أن يحصل الحالف في رتبة المستثنين بعد سنة من حلفه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r12.speaker: الزهراوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r12.claim: Al-Zahrawi says Ibn Abbas discussed a future promise, not an oath whose bond one wants to dissolve.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r12.anchor: إنما تكلم ابن عباس في أن الاستثناء بعد سنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r13.claim: Some jurists attribute to Ibn Abbas the view that a delayed exception cancels expiation, and infer the same for anyone who says a delayed exception is valid.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r13.anchor: وذهبت فرقة من الفقهاء إلى أن مذهب ابن عباس سقوط الكفارة وألزموا كل من يقول ينفع الاستثناء بعد مدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r14.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r14.claim: Malik and others limit an exception to an oath by God, excluding divorce and vows to travel to Mecca; al-Shafiʿi, jurists of opinion, Tawus, and Hammad allow exceptions in those other commitments too.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r14.anchor: وليس الاستثناء إلا في اليمين بالله، لا يكون في طلاق ونحوه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r15.claim: A verbal exception does not help with a deliberately false oath; an exception must itself be spoken aloud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r15.anchor: وليس في اليمين الغموس استثناء ينفع، ولا يكون الاستثناء بالقول،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r16.speaker: محمد الكوفي المفسر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r16.claim: Muhammad al-Kufi says the words 'perhaps my Lord will guide me' are a required formula and expiation for anyone who forgot the exception.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r16.anchor: قال محمد الكوفي المفسر: إنها بألفاظها مما أمر أن يقولها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r17.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r17.claim: Most interpreters treat the phrase as a general supplication, not a formula restricted to making up a forgotten exception.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509/r17.anchor: وقال الجمهور هو دعاء مأمور به دون هذا التخصيص

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the prayer asks God to make a nearer sign of the Prophet's mission clear than the story of the sleepers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r1.anchor: وقال الزجاج المعنى عسى أن ييسر الله من الأدلة على نبوتي أقرب من دليل أصحاب الكهف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r2.claim: The author prefers the broader sense: may God guide the Prophet more rightly in future affairs; although addressed to him, the instruction extends to the community because people often need it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#2/r2.anchor: وما قدمته أصوب، أي عسى أن يرشدني فيما استقبل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r1.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r1.claim: Quraysh asked the Prophet about Dhul-Qarnayn, the Spirit, and the Companions of the Cave; he promised an answer tomorrow without saying God willing, so Gabriel's revelation was delayed fifteen days and he was distressed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r1.anchor: قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r3.claim: Remember your Lord when you forget means remember Him after the lapse of forgetfulness; the example means to tell someone your need after prayer ends.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري معناه واذكر ربك بعد تفضي النسيان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r4.claim: If you forgot to make an exception, say God willing when you remember, even after a day, month, or year.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r4.anchor: أحدها ان المعنى اذا نسيت الاستثناء ثم ذكرت فقل إن شاء الله ولو كان بعد يوم أو شهر أو سنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes إذا نسيت to mean when you become angry; Ibn al-Anbari says this is plausible because anger produces forgetfulness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r5.anchor: والثاني أن معنى إذا نسيت إذا غضبت قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r6.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r6.claim: A third interpretation is to remember God when you forget something so that He will remind you of it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r6.anchor: والثالث إذا نسيت الشيء فاذكر الله ليذكرك إياه حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r7.claim: An exception keeps an oath-taker from lying if the promised act is not done; Moses' exception before his trial is an example.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r7.anchor: وفائدة الاستثناء أن يخرج الحالف من الكذب إذا لم يفعل ما حلف عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r8.speaker: أحمد ومالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r8.claim: Divorce or manumission conditional on God's will still takes effect; the author says this is the transmitted position from Ahmad and Malik's view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r8.anchor: ولا تختلف الرواية عن أحمد أنه لا يصح الاستثناء في الطلاق والعتاق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r9.claim: They hold that neither divorce nor manumission takes effect when made conditional on God's will.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة والشافعي لا يقع شيء من ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r10.claim: An exception is valid in an oath by God and in expiatory forms such as ẓihār and vows; these concern future acts, unlike the operative wording of divorce and manumission.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r10.anchor: وأما اليمين بالله تعالى فان الاستثناء فيها يصح بخلاف الطلاق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r1.speaker: أحمد وأكثر الفقهاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r1.claim: The exception is valid only when joined directly to the oath; this is also reported from Ahmad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r1.anchor: أحدها انه لا يصح الاستثناء الا موصولا بالكلام وقد روي عن أحمد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r2.speaker: الحسن وطاووس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r2.claim: Another view allows an exception as long as the speaker remains in the same gathering; something similar is reported from Ahmad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r2.anchor: والثاني انه يصح ما دام في المجلس قاله الحسن وطاووس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وأبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r3.claim: A third view allows an exception even after a year.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r3.anchor: والثالث انه لو أستثنى بعد سنة جاز قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد ابن جبير وأبو العالية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r4.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r4.claim: Al-Tabari says one may say God willing even after breaking the oath to remove the sin of omitting the exception; expiation remains unless the exception was attached to the oath.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جرير الطبري الصواب للإنسان أن يستثني ولو بعد حنثه في يمينه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r5.claim: Those who allow a year mean that the later exception removes blame for failing to say it, not the required expiation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r5.anchor: أراد سقوط الحرج الذي يلزمه بترك الاسثتناء دون الكفارة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r6.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r6.claim: They pronounce the yāʾ of يهديني in connected recitation but omit it at a pause.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r6.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو عمرو يهديني ربي بياء في الوصل دون الوقف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r7.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r7.claim: He pronounces the yāʾ in both connected and paused recitation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير بياء في الحالين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r8.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r8.claim: They omit the yāʾ in both connected and paused recitation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي بغير ياء في الحالين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r9.claim: One meaning asks God for signs and proof of prophethood clearer than the Cave story; God gave the Prophet knowledge of the unseen of the messengers as clearer evidence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r9.anchor: أحدهما عسى أن يعطيني ربي من الايات والدلالات على النبوة ما يكون أقرب في الرشد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p128/r10.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet asks God to reveal the answers to Quraysh's questions and guide him before the promised time.

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r1.claim: إلا may scope over the prohibition: do not say “I will do it tomorrow” unless God permits that utterance.
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r1.anchor: قاله أبو البقاء: " في المستثنى منه ثلاثة أوجه

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r2.claim: Or it may scope over فاعل: do not claim you will do it without adding إن شاء الله; a third analysis is a disconnected exception.
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r2.anchor: قاله أبو البقاء: " في المستثنى منه ثلاثة أوجه

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r3.claim: أن يشاء may be an exception with وقت omitted (“except when God wills”), or circumstantial with قول omitted (“while saying إن شاء الله”).
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r3.anchor: قاله أبو البقاء: " في المستثنى منه ثلاثة أوجه

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r4.claim: A further estimate supplies بـ: speak while bound by God's will, i.e. while saying إن شاء الله.
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r4.anchor: في المستثنى منه ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects scope over فاعل because that expresses legitimate contingency, outside the prohibition's intended point.
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r5.anchor: قلت: قد رد الزمخشري الوجه الثاني، فقال: " إلا أن يشاء " متعلق بالنهي

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r6.claim: He attaches it to the prohibition as either permission to say the statement or saying it contingent on God's will; a third view makes it mean “never,” as at 7:89.
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r6.anchor: قلت: قد رد الزمخشري الوجه الثاني، فقال: " إلا أن يشاء " متعلق بالنهي

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects the perpetuity interpretation after transmitting it from al-Tabari and others, without explaining the flaw.
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r7.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره الزمخشري قد رده ابن عطية بعد أن حكاه عن الطبري وغيره

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r8.claim: The apparent exception cannot be part of the forbidden statement: “unless God wills” is true and cannot be forbidden.
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r8.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " وإلا أن يشاء الله استثناء لا يمكن حمله على ظاهره

SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:24/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
