ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: it is not appropriate for the Prophet (sws) to given an unconditional commitment in this regard

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: After remembering God, the Prophet may tell those he promised that his Lord may guide him to the right answer before the promised time.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: it may well be that his Lord guides him to the right answer even before the promised time

DURR-FULL:v5p376/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r9.claim: Quraysh consulted Jews about Muhammad, saying they knew no al-Rahman except Musaylima of Yamama; the Jews recognized the expected prophet's description and time.
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد أن قريشا اجتمعت فقالوا: يا محمد قد رغبت عن ديننا ودين آبائنا فما هذا الدين الذي جئت به

STUDYQURAN:18:60/r77.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r77.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r77.claim: The Prophet is likewise advised not to promise future action without acknowledging God’s will.
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r77.anchor: where the Prophet Muhammad is advised never to promise anything in the future without acknowledging God’s Will

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p143/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p143/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p143/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that forty nights after the Prophet swore an oath, the instruction not to promise future action without God's will was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p143/r4.anchor: وأخرجه ابن جرير عن الضحاك وأخرجه ابن مردويه أيضا عن أبن عباس قال حلف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على يمين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p388/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p388/r6.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p388/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr retain yāʾ in yahdinī in connected recitation; Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī omit it.

IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r10.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r10.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r10.claim: The command not to promise an answer for tomorrow refers to the Prophet’s assurance that he would answer their question the next day; he should qualify it with God’s will.
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r10.anchor: ولا تقولن لشيء سألوك عنه كما قلت في هذا: إني مخبركم غدا. واستثن شيئة الله

IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r11.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r11.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r11.claim: When he forgets, the Prophet should remember God and ask for guidance to something better than what they requested, since he does not know what God will do.
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r11.anchor: واذكر ربك إذا نسيت، وقل عسى أن يهدين ربي 18: 24 لخير مما سألتموني عنه رشدا

BURSEVI:v10p162/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p162/r9.claim: He links remembrance through God's name to the command to remember one's Lord when one forgets, since remembrance and forgetting are states of the heart.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r9.anchor: قال تعالى : {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت} فالذكر والنسيان في الحقيقة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r4.claim: Saad appeals to 87:6 and 18:24 to argue that God protected the Prophet from forgetting, so nansa'ha means defer or leave rather than cause him to forget.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r4.anchor: أقول يريد بالتمسك بالآيتين أن الله رفع النسيان

BURHAN:v1p398/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p398/r8.speaker: أبو العباس
BURHAN:v1p398/r8.claim: The guidance in the cave context is spiritual and enabled the Prophet to leave his people with his religion; Moses’ request for guidance to Midian concerns a perceptible route.
BURHAN:v1p398/r8.anchor: سياق الكلام في أمور محسوسة والهداية فيه ملكوتية وقد هداه الله

DAMGHANI:v1p374/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r4.claim: Aqrab can mean more correct or sounder.
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r4.anchor: لأقرب من هذا رشدا أي لأصوب من هذا

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r1.claim: Qasas retains the speaker's yāʾ in yahdīnī because Moses flees Pharaoh in fear and turns wholly to God; Kahf's less urgent prayer omits it, using the kasra instead.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r1.anchor: الخوف يستدعي أن يلصق الإنسان بمن يحميه ويلقي بنفسه كلها عليه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r2.claim: In Qasas, 'Lord' precedes the guidance verb because the fearful speaker first seeks his protector; Kahf foregrounds guidance because its context asks for right direction amid differing views.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r2.anchor: قدم (الرب) على فعل الهداية لأنه هو الملجأ فقال

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r3.claim: The yāʾ pronoun occurs more often in Qasas, and guidance is mentioned twelve times there against five in Kahf; the greater recurrence supports the fuller form in Qasas.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r3.anchor: ثم لننظر من ناحية أخرى فإن ياء الضمير تكرر في (القصص) أكثر مما في الكهف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r4.claim: Qasas tells Moses' story at length, while the Kahf prayer occurs briefly within the sleepers' story; Samarrai links the longer account to the longer verb form and the concise account to deletion.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r4.anchor: مقام التبسط والتطويل في (القصص) في قصة موسى أكثر بكثير مما ورد في (الكهف)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r13.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r13.claim: As another example of retaining or omitting the first-person yā, he contrasts “may guide me” in 18:24 with the explicit yā in 28:22.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r13.anchor: ومن ذلك: أي ذِكْرُ ياءِ المتكلم أو حذفها قوله تعالى: {وَقُلْ عسى أَن يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّي لأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هاذا رَشَداً}
